item.title: California Knows Business-Friendly Rules Stifle Innovation
item.description: California is leading a group of 12 states suing to block Paramount Skydance Corp.’s $110 billion purchase of Warner Bros Discovery Inc., claiming the deal would give the combined company unfair control of movie and cable-TV businesses. Paramount executives responded by threatening to pull its operations out of the Golden State and go to where it’s wanted.
item.dc:creator: Gautam Mukunda

item.title: Acemoglu's New Book Seeks to Restore Liberalism
item.description: Daron Acemoglu’s new book, What Happened to Liberal Democracy?, is deservedly commanding a lot of attention. One of the world’s most eminent economists, the author combines extraordinary historical breadth, cutting-edge technical expertise and a stunning level of academic productivity. He’s co-written excellent popular works on why some countries grew rich and others didn’t, about technology and progress, and about the challenge of creating and sustaining liberty. item.dc:creator: Clive Crook

item.title: The 30-Year Itch Comes for Bonds — and Brazil
item.description: In both cases, investors have cause for concern.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: Why Iran’s New Leaders Need to Continue the War
item.description: Earlier this year, as the Islamic Republic of Iran was busy crushing the largest protests since those in the aftermath of the 1979 revolution, President Donald Trump promised that help was on its way. He meant, of course, that the US would ride to the rescue of the ordinary Iranians being slaughtered in the streets. Instead, he launched a war that’s given a new lease on life to the regime that was killing them.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: AI's Tendency to Lie and Cheat Is Written Into Its Training
item.description: Artificial intelligence models are trained not to lie to humans. Yet a funny thing is happening: AI has been lying to humans quite a bit.
item.dc:creator: Parmy Olson

item.title: UK's Social Care Morass May Be Andy Burnham’s Biggest Test Yet
item.description: Develop brain cancer in England and the National Health Service largely covers you. Get diagnosed with dementia and you may pay until your savings are depleted — and even then some bills keep coming. A parliamentary committee summed up the system as “unfair, confusing, demeaning and frightening.” Some might call that British understatement.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Germany Is Seeking Peace in UniCredit’s Commerzbank Victory
item.description: The German government is finally accepting the inevitable: UniCredit Group SpA has essentially won the battle for Commerzbank AG. The finance ministry still holds a stake in Commerzbank and is seeking a gracious exit after bitterly opposing the Italian takeover. item.dc:creator: Paul J. Davies

item.title: Americans Have More Money, Europeans Better Manners
item.description: People may not be as polite in the US, but they’re richer.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: Trump's Decision to Cancel Korea Military Drills Is a Gift to Kim Jong Un
item.description: The world’s gaze is appropriately focused on conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine. Neither looks to be settled soon, despite a great deal of military action, sporadic diplomatic efforts and ongoing sanctions imposed on both Iran and Russia.
item.dc:creator: James Stavridis

item.title: India Needs Guardrails Around Shadow Loans, Not Bans
item.description: Some of India’s smaller nonbank financiers have been getting a bit too creative lately. And that has led the Reserve Bank of India to consider restricting the access to financing needed by self-employed professionals and small business owners.
item.dc:creator: Andy Mukherjee

item.title: The American Dream Now Comes With a Survival Guide
item.description: The US has never had to try that hard to convince Asia’s brightest to come to its shores — the allure of a better life and promising economic opportunities has been difficult to resist. But President Donald Trump’s latest immigration restrictions are shifting perspectives. The American dream hasn’t disappeared for international students — now it just comes with a survival guide.
item.dc:creator: Karishma Vaswani

item.title: Gareth Edwards’ Jurassic World Exit Shows Hollywood’s Director Problem
item.description: For the next stage of its evolution, the Jurassic World franchise will have to find a way with a new director. News recently broke that Jurassic World Rebirth director Gareth Edwards won’t be returning for the follow-up, with the Hollywood Reporter citing “creative differences” as the reason for his exit. item.dc:creator: Matthew A. Winkler

item.title: Harry Sargeant's Venezuela Oil Exit Offers Clues About Country's Next Phase
item.description: Six months after Energy Secretary Chris Wright pledged that the US-Venezuela partnership would lead to a “dramatic increase” in oil, natural gas and electricity production, the gusher has yet to gush.
item.dc:creator: Juan Pablo Spinetto

item.title: Gen Z Is Mistaking Sports Betting for Investing
item.description: If the bad news is that members of Generation Z can’t afford to buy a house until they are middle-aged — which isn’t really bad news, honestly, but anyway — then the good news is that at least they are investing their money in high-performing assets. Or so we thought. Now we are learning that they might not be very good investors, or even investors at all: According to a new survey, more than half redirected funds to sports gambling, which a quarter consider to be part of a long-term investment
item.dc:creator: Allison Schrager

item.title: Pentagon Budget Should Be Subject to Bipartisan Fiscal Scrutiny
item.description: The White House has chosen an unconventional route to seek a record $1.5 trillion defense budget for 2027 — a nearly 40% real increase from this year. If successful, the strategy would reduce oversight of Pentagon spending and the need for bipartisan compromise. That’s precisely why Congress should resist it.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Gas Prices Hurt Pickup Truck Drivers. That's a Republican Problem
item.description: High gas prices are squeezing all Americans in some way. But the spike in oil prices from the Iran War is hitting no one harder than people who drive pickup trucks. And that could prove a wildcard in the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Brownstein
